The prototype Strike Suit mounts a Clan-specification Advanced SRM-3 launcher with three shots, delivering greater effective range and hitting power than the production model's Inner Sphere equivalent. A Light TAG system in the left arm provides target designation capability, and both arms end in Battle Claws rather than the production model's Basic Manipulators. The Anti-Personnel Weapon Mount is retained.

Mixed Clan and Inner Sphere technology classifies the prototype as experimental. The 450 kilograms of standard armor and ground-only movement profile match the production model, but the Clan launcher must be jettisoned before anti-BattleMech attacks can be performed. The dependence on Clan-sourced components limited the prototype's operational availability and complicated logistics for any unit fielding the suit alongside Inner Sphere standard equipment.

The production Gray Death Strike Suit mounts a detachable SRM-3 launcher with two reloads as its primary armament, paired with a Light TAG system for designating targets for friendly artillery and semi-guided munitions. Basic Manipulators replace the prototype's Battle Claws, and an Anti-Personnel Weapon Mount handles infantry-scale threats. The launcher can be jettisoned after expenditure, slightly improving the suit's ground speed and allowing the trooper to continue contributing as a forward observer through the TAG system.

At 1,000 kilograms with 450 kilograms of standard armor, the Strike Suit is a well-protected medium platform. It lacks jump capability entirely, relying on a powerful ground movement system that reaches 32 km/h over open terrain. The absence of jump jets limits the suit's tactical flexibility in rough terrain but simplifies maintenance and reduces the training burden on new troopers. The Strike operates best in a fire support role, softening targets with missiles before heavier forces close the distance.

text.deployment: Clan Points carrying the micro pulse laser variant of the Fire configuration filled a niche as precision strikers in high-temperature environments. Five troopers could engage specific targets within burning structures without the collateral concerns of flamer or ballistic weapons, making this configuration the preferred choice when Falcon commanders needed to secure objectives intact rather than simply destroy them.

Word of Blake Level I teams equipped with the micro pulse laser Fire variant served in facility seizure operations during the Jihad. Six troopers with fire-resistant armor and precision energy weapons could breach burning installations, neutralize defenders with targeted fire, and secure critical equipment or data stores before the flames consumed them.

Inner Sphere naval infantry organized captured Space-configured Elementals into four-trooper boarding squads. The flamer proved effective in the confined corridors of DropShips and space stations, where its area effect could sweep compartments without risking hull breaches that ballistic weapons might cause. Four troopers provided sufficient mass to secure individual deck sections during boarding actions.

Clan Snow Raven developed the Space configuration in 2903, and Raven Points have served as the primary operators throughout its history. Five-trooper Points carrying flamers for shipboard engagements formed the backbone of Snow Raven marine contingents. The flamer's utility in zero-gravity corridor fighting, combined with the Space suit's extended life support and hull-breaching cutting torch, made Raven boarding Points among the most feared naval infantry in Clan space.

ComStar naval forces organized Space-configured Elementals into six-trooper Level I boarding teams for WarShip and space station security operations. The larger formation allowed Com Guard commanders to split teams into two three-trooper fire elements during corridor-by-corridor clearance, maintaining momentum through multi-deck boarding actions while the flamer's area effect cleared compartments efficiently.

Inner Sphere naval forces fielding the machine gun Space variant used four-trooper squads for defensive shipboard security rather than offensive boarding. The machine gun provided effective anti-personnel firepower for repelling boarders, while the Space suit's zero-gravity capability allowed troopers to reposition quickly through unpressurized sections to reinforce threatened areas of a vessel.

Snow Raven Points carrying the machine gun Space variant typically served in defensive naval roles, protecting Raven WarShips and transport vessels from hostile boarding actions. Five troopers with machine guns stationed at key chokepoints within a vessel could deliver withering fire against attackers funneled through airlocks and corridors. The Raven fleet's emphasis on aerospace superiority made these defensive marine Points an essential complement to their capital ships.

Word of Blake naval forces employed six-trooper Level I teams carrying the machine gun Space variant for shipboard security aboard their extensive WarShip fleet. The larger formation size allowed Blakist commanders to establish layered defensive zones within vessels, with pairs of troopers covering each approach to critical ship systems such as engineering spaces, bridges, and weapons bays.

Inner Sphere squads equipped with the micro pulse laser Space variant operated in sensitive shipboard environments where precision mattered. Four troopers with accurate energy weapons could engage hostile boarders in compartments containing volatile equipment or munitions, where missed shots from ballistic weapons risked catastrophic secondary damage to the vessel.

Snow Raven Points carrying the micro pulse laser Space configuration served as elite boarding teams for operations against defended targets. Introduced in 3066, the micro pulse laser's accuracy in the tight confines of shipboard combat gave five-trooper Points the ability to neutralize individual defenders without damaging the vessel or cargo they were attempting to capture. Raven commanders reserved these Points for high-value seizure operations where destroying the target would defeat the purpose of the boarding action.

ComStar Level I formations equipped with the micro pulse laser Space variant served aboard HPG relay stations and orbital facilities where precision engagement was critical. Six troopers could secure sensitive communications equipment and data vaults during boarding defense, neutralizing intruders without risking the irreplaceable technology that justified the facility's defense in the first place.

Society cells equipped with the anti-personnel gauss rifle valued its combination of range and precision. Three-trooper teams conducting targeted elimination missions used the weapon's superior ballistic performance to engage specific individuals from distances that kept the operators beyond effective return fire from conventional weapons.

Inner Sphere squads that obtained the anti-personnel gauss rifle configuration deployed it as a premium anti-infantry option. Four-trooper squads carrying the gauss weapon could engage targets at ranges exceeding most other Elemental armament options, giving IS commanders a standoff capability against defended positions.

Society cells operating in three-trooper teams favored the flamer for its utility in both combat and laboratory defense. The smaller formation size allowed each trooper to cover a wider arc during facility security operations, where the flamer's area-denial properties proved effective in channeling attackers through prepared kill zones.

ComStar and Word of Blake Level I formations fielded six-trooper teams of flamer-equipped Elementals primarily in facility defense roles. The larger formation size allowed Com Guard commanders to establish overlapping fields of fire that made approaching defended positions extremely hazardous for unarmored infantry and light vehicles alike.

Society three-trooper teams carrying the heavy machine gun used the weapon's increased firepower to compensate for their smaller formation size. The heavier caliber rounds allowed each trooper to deliver substantially more damage against lightly armored targets than a standard machine gun, partially offsetting the reduced number of suits in the formation.

Inner Sphere squads armed with the heavy machine gun configuration leveraged the weapon's stopping power in counter-insurgency operations. Four troopers carrying the heavier weapon could dominate engagements against militia forces and pirates with greater authority than standard machine gun-equipped formations, making the configuration popular among garrison commands.

The heavy machine gun became available to Clan Elementals in 3059, offering greater lethality against soft targets than the standard machine gun. Five-trooper Points armed with the heavy variant deliver punishing volumes of fire that can suppress or destroy conventional infantry platoons in seconds. The weapon's increased caliber also provides marginal effectiveness against light vehicle armor, giving these Points limited capability against threats that would otherwise require missile engagement. Clan warriors consider the heavy machine gun a strong choice for anti-infantry specialists operating in combined-arms formations.

Word of Blake Level I teams armed with heavy machine guns served as area-suppression specialists during the Jihad. Six troopers with the heavier weapon could blanket an engagement zone with devastating firepower, making these formations particularly feared in urban combat where Blakist forces frequently engaged irregular defenders.

Society three-trooper teams equipped with the small laser configuration valued its reliability and independence from ammunition supply lines. Operating in isolation from mainstream Clan logistics, the Society's preference for energy weapons reflected their need for sustained operational capability without resupply.

Inner Sphere squads equipped with the laser configuration appreciated the weapon's simplicity and zero ammunition dependency. Four-trooper squads conducting extended patrols or garrison duty could operate for prolonged periods without logistical support, making the laser a popular choice among IS commanders unfamiliar with Clan supply practices.

The small laser has served as a standard Elemental weapon option since the suit's earliest deployments. Clan Points carrying the laser configuration excel in sustained engagements where ammunition conservation matters, as the energy weapon draws directly from the suit's power supply. This makes laser-equipped Points particularly effective during extended campaigns or deep raids where resupply is uncertain. Many Clan garrison formations default to the laser for routine patrol and security duties.

ComStar Level I formations equipped with the laser configuration leveraged the weapon's ammunition independence during garrison operations across their extensive network of HPG compounds. Six troopers carrying energy weapons could maintain a defensive posture indefinitely, an attractive proposition for facilities far from established military supply chains.

Society teams carrying the machine gun configuration employed them in anti-personnel roles, particularly against conventional infantry defending research facilities targeted for seizure. Three-trooper teams provided sufficient suppressive fire to pin defending forces while Society operatives completed their objectives.

Inner Sphere squads fielding the machine gun option found it effective for counter-insurgency and anti-infantry operations. The four-trooper squad could deliver a devastating volume of fire against soft targets, and IS logistics personnel found machine gun ammunition far easier to source than Clan-standard energy weapon components.

Machine gun-equipped Points serve as anti-infantry specialists within Clan formations. The weapon's high rate of fire makes five-trooper Points carrying this configuration lethal against conventional infantry concentrations, scout vehicles, and unarmored assets. Clan commanders frequently deploy machine gun Points in screening roles, where their ability to shred light targets allows heavier assets to focus on armored opposition. The configuration sees extensive use in garrison and counter-insurgency operations across occupied territories.

Word of Blake Militia formations made extensive use of machine gun-equipped Elemental Level I teams during the Jihad. Six troopers carrying machine guns could suppress large areas of enemy infantry, and the Blakists employed these formations in urban clearing operations where their fire volume overwhelmed conventional defenders.

Society teams adopted the micro pulse laser shortly after its introduction, valuing the weapon's accuracy at close range. Three-trooper cells conducting targeted strikes against enemy command elements found the micro pulse laser's precision allowed them to engage individual targets without the collateral effects of area weapons.

ComStar Level I formations adopted the micro pulse laser for security operations requiring precision engagement capability. Six-trooper teams carrying the accurate energy weapon could neutralize threats in sensitive environments where collateral damage posed unacceptable risk, such as HPG stations and command centers.

Inner Sphere forces gained limited access to the Elemental II through salvage and trade during the latter Dark Age period. Four-trooper squads valued the suit's ground speed for rapid response operations across the sprawling urban environments of the former Clan Occupation Zone, where the ability to keep pace with wheeled vehicles outweighed the loss of jump mobility that characterized the original Elemental.

Clan Hell's Horses Points are the primary operators of the Elemental II, fielding it in large numbers alongside their vehicle and BattleMech formations. Five-trooper Points exploit the suit's ground speed to maintain pace with combined-arms advances, repositioning rapidly between engagements without relying on OmniMech transport. Horses commanders pair Elemental II Points with fast-moving armor columns, using the troopers to secure objectives and clear buildings that vehicles cannot enter. The Easy to Maintain design quirk has made the suit popular with Horses logistics personnel, who appreciate its simplified field servicing requirements compared to the original Elemental.

Six-trooper formations operating the Elemental II have been documented in limited numbers among Republic Armed Forces units that inherited equipment from former Clan occupation zones. The Level I organization persisted in some garrison formations during the late Republic and early ilClan periods, though the suit's association with Hell's Horses limited its broader adoption outside territories directly bordering Horses holdings.

No confirmed Inner Sphere four-trooper deployments of the Elemental II prototype exist. The handful of suits produced at Transitional Facility A-4 remained exclusively within Hell's Horses testing programs, though the four-trooper organizational table was maintained for contingency planning should salvaged suits reach non-Clan forces operating in the Horses' border regions.

Hell's Horses engineers tested the Elemental II prototype in standard five-trooper Points during evaluation trials on Csesztreg. Only a small number of suits were produced at the mobile Transitional Facility A-4, and these saw limited operational deployment against pirates raiding the Horses' capital enclave. The prototype's poor reputation among Clan warriors, stemming from its inability to perform anti-BattleMech attacks and the awkward requirement to jettison its main weapon before reaching top speed, ensured that test Points were composed of volunteers rather than assigned personnel.

No six-trooper formations of the Elemental II prototype have been documented. The experimental nature of the design and its extremely limited production run of only a handful of suits precluded distribution beyond the Horses' own testing programs. The organizational table exists for completeness, reflecting the theoretical possibility of non-Clan forces organizing salvaged prototypes into Level I formations.

Hell's Horses Points carrying the anti-personnel gauss rifle variant of the Elemental III serve as advance screening elements for combined-arms formations. Five troopers equipped with stealth armor and the longest-ranged weapon option available can infiltrate forward positions undetected and engage enemy scouts and observation posts from concealment. Horses commanders use these Points to establish a sensor-proof forward screen that denies enemy reconnaissance while maintaining their own situational awareness.

Six-trooper formations fielding the Elemental III with anti-personnel gauss rifles have appeared in small numbers among successor organizations that inherited the Level I structure. The combination of stealth armor and standoff weaponry makes these formations well-suited to installation security, where six troopers with reduced signatures can establish an undetectable perimeter around sensitive facilities.

Inner Sphere squads equipping the Elemental III with micro pulse lasers operated as precision strike teams. Four troopers with stealth armor and accurate energy weapons could infiltrate enemy positions, eliminate specific high-value targets such as communication equipment or command personnel, and exfiltrate before the enemy could organize a response.

The support variant's King David configuration entered CCAF service in four-trooper squads following the 3074 introduction. These squads provided precision ranged fire support that the original mine-focused Fa Shih lacked, filling a gap in Capellan battle armor capability until the Trinity series became widely available.

The support variant's King David configuration in five-trooper Points saw limited circulation among Clan forces. As a later production variant introduced during the Jihad era, fewer of these suits reached Clan hands through salvage, and those that did typically served in rear-area security formations rather than frontline combat.

The King David support variant in six-trooper Level I formations offered precision fire support at the squad level. Blakist and Com Guard commanders valued the light gauss rifle's range and accuracy, and the larger formation size allowed these Level I units to deliver sustained long-range volleys that smaller squads could not match.

Plasma-equipped support squads served as anti-vehicle specialists within CCAF four-trooper formations. The plasma rifle's ability to generate heat buildup in targeted machines made these squads particularly effective when operating against BattleMechs in conjunction with conventional Capellan armor and infantry.

Plasma-armed Fa Shih suits in Clan five-trooper Points were rare acquisitions. The plasma rifle's heat-generation capability against BattleMechs offered tactical utility that some Clan garrison commanders found useful, though the suit's overall specifications fell well below Clan standards for dedicated anti-BattleMech battle armor.

Plasma-armed Fa Shih suits in six-trooper Level I formations served as anti-vehicle specialists within Blakist and Com Guard force structures. Six plasma rifles concentrated on a single target could generate dangerous heat spikes in enemy BattleMechs, making these formations a serious threat during close-range engagements.

Capellan Confederation Armed Forces organized Fa Shih troopers into standard four-trooper squads, matching Inner Sphere infantry doctrine. Flamer-equipped squads typically operated in augmented lances alongside BattleMech or armor formations, using their mine-laying and incendiary capability to shape the battlefield ahead of heavier assets. Warrior House infantry battalions integrated these squads into their combined-arms formations.

Five-trooper Points of Fa Shih battle armor reflected Clan organizational doctrine applied to captured or salvaged Capellan equipment. Clan forces operating near the Confederation's borders occasionally acquired small numbers of these suits, incorporating them into garrison Clusters where their mine-laying capability supplemented defensive positions.

Word of Blake technical advisors who assisted in developing the Fa Shih retained familiarity with the design, and Blakist militia units organized captured or acquired suits into six-trooper Level I formations. Flamer-equipped Level I units leveraged the larger formation size to saturate defensive zones with both mines and incendiary fire.

Four-trooper squads carrying the laser loadout served as general-purpose battle armor within CCAF formations. The energy weapon's reliability made these squads preferred for extended operations where ammunition resupply was uncertain. CCAF infantry platoons composed of four such squads provided a flexible screen for Capellan BattleMech lances.

Clan units that acquired Fa Shih suits organized them into standard five-trooper Points in accordance with Clan formation doctrine. Laser-configured suits offered a familiar energy weapon platform that required minimal logistical adjustment, though Clan warriors generally considered the design inferior to purpose-built Clan battle armor.

ComStar and Word of Blake forces organized Fa Shih suits into six-trooper Level I formations per their military doctrine. Laser-configured Level I units provided a self-contained energy weapon team with fifty percent more troopers than a standard Capellan squad, increasing both firepower density and survivability during sustained engagements.

Light recoilless rifle squads offered Capellan commanders a ranged ballistic option within standard four-trooper formations. These squads often deployed at greater standoff distances than their flamer or laser counterparts, providing covering fire while mine-laying squads prepared defensive positions ahead of advancing enemy forces.

Points of light recoilless rifle-equipped Fa Shih represented an uncommon sight among Clan formations. Where these suits appeared in Clan service, they typically filled second-line garrison roles, with the five-trooper Point structure providing slightly more firepower per formation than Inner Sphere squads.

Six-trooper Level I formations equipped with light recoilless rifles offered Com Guard and Blakist commanders a ranged fire support element that could operate independently of heavier assets. The additional two troopers beyond standard Inner Sphere squad size allowed these formations to sustain casualties while maintaining combat effectiveness.

Machine gun squads proved effective in anti-infantry and garrison roles across CCAF deployments. Four-trooper squads equipped with this configuration frequently supported Capellan conventional infantry during urban sweeps and perimeter defense operations, where rapid-fire capability against soft targets was more valuable than anti-armor firepower.

Machine gun-equipped Fa Shih suits organized into five-trooper Clan Points served primarily in anti-infantry and security roles. The additional trooper per formation compared to Inner Sphere squads increased the volume of suppressive fire available, though Clan commanders rarely committed these captured suits to frontline engagements.

Machine gun-armed Fa Shih suits in six-trooper Level I formations excelled at perimeter security and anti-infantry screening. Word of Blake militia units employed these formations to defend installations and supply lines, where the combination of mine-laying capability and high-volume suppressive fire created formidable defensive positions.

TAG-equipped four-trooper squads operated as forward observer teams within CCAF combined-arms formations. Paired with Arrow IV-equipped artillery or semi-guided missile carriers, these squads leveraged the Fa Shih's jump capability and magnetic clamps to reach observation positions inaccessible to conventional spotters, calling precision strikes onto hardened targets.

Five-trooper Points carrying TAG equipment represented a niche application of the Fa Shih within Clan force structures. The target designation capability held limited appeal for Clan warriors who favored direct engagement, though some garrison commanders recognized the value of coordinated indirect fire for defensive operations.

TAG-equipped Level I formations of six troopers provided Word of Blake and Com Guard artillery batteries with dedicated forward observer teams. The larger formation size allowed Level I commanders to split their unit into observer and security elements, maintaining target designation capability even under direct enemy contact.

The four experimental Fa Shih 2 suits were organized into a single demonstration squad by Ceres Metals for Strategios evaluation. Field simulations on Capella showed marked improvement in anti-BattleMech performance, with the myomer-boosted troopers tearing through significantly more armor during swarm attacks than standard Fa Shih operators.

The Fa Shih 2's Clan myomer booster technology made the experimental suit a peculiar candidate for Clan Point organization. With only four suits ever produced, no complete five-trooper Point of this variant could be formed, making this configuration a theoretical formation for contingency planning rather than an operational reality.

The experimental Fa Shih 2 was never produced in sufficient numbers to equip a six-trooper Level I formation. With only four suits manufactured by Ceres Metals, the Clan myomer booster variant remained confined to Capellan evaluation programs and did not enter ComStar or Word of Blake service in any organizational structure.

The extended-range medium laser configuration entered LAAF service during the later stages of the FedCom Civil War. Four-trooper squads valued the increased engagement distance, which allowed them to harass armored targets from positions where the Fenrir's light armor was less of a liability, particularly in open terrain.

Five-trooper Points equipped with ER medium laser Fenrirs served in limited numbers among Lyran units adopting Clan organizational structures. The extended range gave Point-strength formations standoff capability against opposing battle armor and light vehicles during border defense operations.

Word of Blake forces organized ER medium laser Fenrirs into Level I units during Jihad operations on Lyran worlds. The six-trooper formation's combined long-range fire provided effective harassment and overwatch capability in support of heavier Blakist formations.

The machine gun loadout saw extensive use with LAAF infantry squads during garrison operations and the FedCom Civil War. Four-trooper squads assigned to planetary militia and second-line regiments used the configuration for base security, convoy escort, and anti-insurgency patrols, where its volume of fire against unarmored targets proved highly effective.

Clan-organized forces fielding captured or salvaged Fenrir suits in five-trooper Points found the machine gun configuration useful for rear-area security duties. The configuration's anti-infantry focus aligned well with garrison roles where Points could suppress conventional resistance without expending more valuable resources.

Word of Blake Militia formations organized captured Fenrir suits into six-trooper Level I units during the Jihad. The machine gun configuration served in urban pacification roles on occupied Lyran worlds, where the larger formation size compensated for the suit's light armor in contested environments.

Mortar-configured Fenrir squads filled an indirect fire role within LAAF infantry companies. Four-trooper squads provided organic fire support, lobbing mortar rounds over obstacles while the machine gun secondary armament defended against close-range threats. The configuration saw growing use during the Jihad as urban fighting increased the demand for indirect fire platforms.

Five-trooper Points of mortar-equipped Fenrirs saw limited deployment among irregular forces using Clan organizational patterns. The indirect fire capability gave Point-strength formations a suppressive tool unavailable to most battle armor units, though sustained mortar fire depleted ammunition quickly.

Word of Blake Militia Level I units fielded mortar Fenrirs during Jihad urban operations. The six-trooper formation could maintain a steady rate of indirect fire, suppressing defensive positions and denying terrain to opposing infantry while heavier Blakist assets maneuvered into position.

Medium pulse laser Fenrir squads served as dedicated anti-vehicle elements within LAAF infantry companies. Four-trooper squads coordinated their fire to threaten light combat vehicles and hover tanks, and a full squad concentrating fire could damage even medium-weight BattleMechs during the FedCom Civil War.

Five-trooper Points of medium pulse laser Fenrirs appeared among garrison forces on Lyran worlds bordering Clan occupation zones. The heavier weapon gave Point-strength formations a credible threat against Clan vehicles and second-line BattleMechs encountered during border skirmishes.

ComStar Com Guard Level I units occasionally integrated medium pulse laser Fenrirs into combined-arms formations. The six-trooper unit's concentrated medium pulse fire provided a meaningful anti-armor contribution to Level II task forces during peacekeeping and defensive operations.

Small laser-equipped Fenrir squads served across LAAF frontline regiments as a versatile anti-infantry and anti-battle armor option. Four-trooper squads valued the energy weapons' independence from ammunition resupply, particularly during extended operations on contested worlds during the Civil War and Jihad.

Five-trooper Points of salvaged small laser Fenrirs appeared in limited numbers among mercenary commands operating under Clan-influenced organizational structures. The ammunition-free loadout reduced logistical demands for units lacking steady supply lines.

ComStar and Word of Blake Level I formations occasionally fielded small laser Fenrirs acquired through Lyran trade agreements or battlefield salvage. The six-trooper formation provided concentrated energy weapon fire without ammunition concerns, suiting the Com Guards' emphasis on self-sufficient tactical units.

The small pulse laser configuration equipped LAAF squads tasked with anti-battle armor operations. Four-trooper squads used the improved accuracy of pulse weapons to engage fast-moving enemy battlesuits during the FedCom Civil War, particularly in urban environments where targets appeared and disappeared rapidly.

Five-trooper Points using pulse laser Fenrirs saw limited service among Lyran-affiliated units that adopted Clan organizational patterns following the Clan Invasion. The improved hit probability against agile targets made the configuration a reasonable choice for Point-strength formations facing Clan battle armor.

Word of Blake Militia Level I units fielded pulse laser Fenrirs in small numbers during Jihad-era operations. The six-trooper formation's concentrated pulse fire proved effective against opposing battle armor in close-quarters engagements on occupied worlds.

SRM-equipped Fenrir squads became one of the LAAF's preferred anti-armor configurations during the FedCom Civil War. Four-trooper squads delivering coordinated missile volleys could cripple light vehicles in a single salvo, and the configuration earned a fearsome reputation among Allied forces facing Lyran battle armor for the first time.

Five-trooper Points fielding the SRM configuration saw use among mercenary and irregular forces organized along Clan lines. The additional trooper added a fifth launcher to each volley, increasing the Point's ability to threaten armored targets, though ammunition supply remained a persistent concern for non-Lyran operators.

Word of Blake Militia Level I units equipped with SRM Fenrirs deployed during the Jihad as heavy assault elements in urban combat. The six-trooper formation could unleash twenty-four missiles in a single coordinated volley, sufficient to threaten medium-weight BattleMechs and devastate lighter targets.

The AFFS organized Fusiliers into standard four-trooper squads and deployed them as line units within battle armor battalions. The suit saw its heaviest use along the Capellan border, where squads integrated into combined-arms task groups for garrison duty and defensive operations. The Fusilier's lack of specialization made it a flexible addition to squad-level formations, filling gaps that more focused designs could not cover without leaving capability holes elsewhere in the unit.

Clan warriors organized captured Fusiliers into five-trooper Points following standard Clan doctrine. The suit's availability along the Clan-Davion border made it a viable salvage acquisition, though its slow speed and Inner Sphere technology limited its appeal compared to purpose-built Clan designs. Points equipped with the Fusilier typically drew garrison or second-line assignments rather than frontline Touman duty.

Republic Armed Forces units organized Fusiliers into six-trooper Level I formations consistent with ComStar-derived military doctrine. The Republic's proximity to Federated Suns manufacturing made procurement straightforward before Fortress Republic sealed the borders. Level I Fusilier teams served in urban garrison roles where the suit's stealth protection and adequate firepower provided a capable security presence.
text.battleHistory:
General Motors began manufacturing the Fusilier at their Salem plant in the early 3120s, producing a suit that filled no particular gap in the AFFS order of battle. The Department of the Quartermaster even so procured the design, and GM continued production for over a decade before introducing an upgraded variant after the Blackout. The Fusilier drew on design elements from both the Grenadier and the Sea Fox, producing a competent if unremarkable assault suit that earned a reputation for solid construction rather than any defining tactical specialty.

Capellan March Militia units developed a marked preference for the original model over the upgrade. A 3139 raid conducted by a New Syrtis CMM detachment on the training world of Nihal demonstrated the reason clearly: when both variants came under fire inside a collapsing structure, the upgraded suits crumpled under falling debris while the original models completed the mission and escaped. The incident reinforced a broader reluctance among frontline units to adopt the newer variant. Warrior House Ijori also acquired captured Fusiliers and employed them on raids across formerly Davion worlds, proving the suit capable even in Capellan hands.

text.deployment: AFFS four-trooper squads received the upgraded Fusilier beginning in the mid-3130s. The revised armament gave squad-level engagements a thermal punch the original lacked, and teams operating against energy-weapon-heavy opponents appreciated the specialized armor protection. Squads deployed along the Capellan border found the reduced jump range a more significant limitation than the armor change, as rapid repositioning often proved critical during small-unit actions.

text.deployment: Clan Points operating captured upgraded Fusiliers found the revised armament more appealing than the original configuration, though the suit's fragile armor remained a significant liability by Clan standards. Five-trooper Points assigned to raiding or border skirmish duties occasionally fielded the upgrade when salvage made it available, but the design saw no widespread Clan adoption.

Republic Armed Forces Level I formations that operated the upgraded Fusilier employed the suit's thermal weapon as a deterrent in garrison and checkpoint operations. Six-trooper teams provided additional firepower density that partially offset the suit's reduced jump capability, though the armor's vulnerability to conventional weapons made Level I commanders cautious about deploying these teams in heavily contested urban environments.

Inner Sphere mercenary commands and corporate garrison forces adopted the Gladiator-S in standard four-trooper squads. StarCorps marketed the suit to smaller outfits unable to afford dedicated battle armor, positioning it as a cost-effective alternative for garrison duty and low-intensity operations. Several corporate security firms operating in semi-hostile frontier environments purchased small batches for perimeter defense and facility protection.

Clan forces have shown no interest in the Gladiator-S. The suit's light armor protection and limited weapon loadout fall far below Clan standards for powered infantry, and its origins as a commercialized arena design carry no appeal for Clan warriors. The five-trooper Point configuration exists for organizational purposes but lacks documented operational deployment.

The Gladiator-S saw limited adoption by ComStar-affiliated security forces in the post-Jihad period, organized into six-trooper Level I formations for facility defense and internal security roles. The suit's low training requirements and modest cost made it accessible to garrison units that lacked the budget or technical support infrastructure for frontline battle armor.

Inner Sphere forces organizing LRM Gnomes into four-trooper squads employed them as fire support elements attached to conventional infantry platoons or BattleMech lances. The stand-off capability allowed squads to contribute indirect fire from positions that kept the heavy suits out of direct close combat.

Clan Hell's Horses developed the LRM configuration from field experience, and five-trooper Points equipped with the variant served as dedicated fire support within combined-arms Stars. The launcher allowed Points to engage targets at ranges previously beyond a Gnome formation's reach, while the anti-personnel weapon discouraged conventional infantry from pressing close. Horse commanders typically positioned LRM Gnome Points behind assault elements, providing covering fire as heavier formations advanced.

ComStar and Word of Blake Level I formations employing LRM Gnomes used the six-trooper unit size to generate concentrated long-range missile fire, providing fire support capability comparable to a light vehicle element at extended ranges.

The three-trooper formation is associated with the Society, whose clandestine operations employed smaller tactical teams suited to covert and unconventional action. Society cells acquired Gnome suits through their embedded positions within Clan scientific and military establishments, fielding them in non-standard formations outside normal Clan doctrine.

Inner Sphere forces gained access to Clan battle armor technology through battlefield salvage, captured manufacturing data, and defections over the course of the post-Invasion era. Those commands that acquired Gnome suits organized them into four-trooper squads consistent with standard Inner Sphere infantry doctrine. The suit's heavy armor and fixed armament made it a straightforward addition to IS battle armor formations, requiring minimal doctrinal adaptation beyond the organizational shift from Clan Points.

ComStar and Word of Blake formations organized battle armor into six-trooper Level I units. Those commands that obtained Gnome suits through salvage or Clan contacts fielded them in this larger formation size, providing additional firepower per tactical unit compared to the standard Clan Point.

Inner Sphere forces that acquired the Bearhunter Upgrade organized them into standard four-trooper squads. The configuration's short-range autocannon armament proved well-suited to close-quarters urban fighting, a scenario where Inner Sphere commanders frequently employed captured Clan battle armor.

Clan Hell's Horses deployed the Bearhunter Upgrade in five-trooper Points specifically tasked with countering heavy and assault-weight battle armor. The configuration's development was driven by encounters with the Ghost Bear Golem, and Horse commanders assigned Bearhunter-equipped Points to formations operating in sectors where Ghost Bear opposition was expected. The variant's short engagement range demanded aggressive Point-level tactics to close distance rapidly.

ComStar and Word of Blake Level I formations using the Bearhunter configuration benefited from the additional two troopers per unit, partially offsetting the variant's limited range by increasing the volume of close-range fire a single tactical element could deliver.

Inner Sphere squads equipped with the Pulse Laser configuration found the variant well-suited to anti-infantry security operations. The micro pulse lasers' accuracy against fast-moving targets made four-trooper squads effective in perimeter defense and convoy escort roles.

Hell's Horses Points fielding the Pulse Laser variant typically operated in a screening role, providing anti-infantry and anti-battle armor coverage for heavier formations. The micro pulse lasers' rapid-fire capability made five-trooper Points effective at suppressing enemy battle armor attempting to close on friendly BattleMechs, an application that complemented the roles filled by standard Gnome or Bearhunter Points.

Word of Blake and ComStar Level I units operating Pulse Laser Gnomes leveraged the six-trooper formation's concentrated firepower for area suppression, where the larger unit size enhanced the variant's anti-personnel strengths.

Hell's Horses commands fielded Fast Assault Golems in four-trooper squads for rapid strike operations within their Inner Sphere territories. The squad's jump capability made it effective for seizing elevated positions and conducting vertical assaults on fortified structures, roles where the standard Golem's lack of jump jets left tactical gaps.

Five-trooper Fast Assault Points served as the primary shock element in Hell's Horses formations. Clan commanders valued the variant's ability to leap into defended positions, bypassing obstacles that pinned down heavier Golem configurations. These Points frequently operated in tandem with Rock Golem Points, combining ranged suppression with aggressive jump assaults.

Like other Horses-produced Golem variants, the Fast Assault saw virtually no deployment in six-trooper Level I formations. The suit remained firmly within Clan Hell's Horses inventories, and the limited production run at Nouveaux Paris further restricted any potential spread to non-Clan operators.

Clan Hell's Horses organized Rock Golem troopers into four-member squads for operations within their Inner Sphere occupation zones. These squads leveraged the variant's extended engagement range for perimeter defense and area denial, where the detachable weapon packs could be positioned to cover key approaches before an engagement began.

Hell's Horses Clusters deployed Rock Golem Points as fire support elements within combined-arms Stars. The variant's longer-ranged armament allowed five-trooper Points to engage targets at distances where standard Golems could not, providing suppressive fire while faster units closed to contact. Points operating in open terrain proved particularly effective in this overwatch role.

The Rock Golem saw negligible adoption outside Clan Hell's Horses and allied Clan forces. Any examples organized into six-trooper Level I formations would have been limited to isolated acquisitions by ComStar or Word of Blake commands operating near Clan occupation zones, with no documented widespread deployment in this squad configuration.

Ghost Bear Dominion garrisons organized Golem troopers into four-member squads when operating alongside Inner Sphere-pattern conventional infantry formations. This squad structure facilitated integration with existing Dominion militia units and proved effective for garrison duty, where smaller teams could cover more ground than a full Clan Point while maintaining sufficient firepower for security operations.

Five-trooper Golem Points became a common sight among Ghost Bear frontline Clusters after 3070. Deployed alongside Elemental Points within combined-arms Stars, Golem Points typically anchored the formation's assault element, using their heavy armor and firepower to spearhead attacks or hold critical positions while lighter battle armor maneuvered on the flanks.

Six-trooper Golem formations saw extremely limited use outside Clan and Dominion forces. ComStar and Word of Blake units that acquired examples organized them into Level I formations consistent with Com Guard doctrine, though the small numbers available meant these formations were rare and typically reserved for specialized garrison or security assignments.

Rasalhague Dominion garrison forces organized Support Golems into four-trooper squads tailored for urban pacification missions. These squads provided sustained missile fire in support of larger combined-arms formations clearing built-up areas, where the suit's ammunition depth allowed prolonged operations without resupply.

Ghost Bear and later Rasalhague Dominion Clusters integrated Support Golem Points into garrison and urban security formations. Five-trooper Points assigned to urban combat duties carried enough ordnance to sustain extended building-clearing operations, and their fire-resistant armor proved valuable in environments where incendiary hazards were common.

The Support Golem's production was limited to a single Ghost Bear facility on Alshain, restricting its availability almost entirely to Ghost Bear and Rasalhague Dominion forces. Six-trooper formations following ComStar organizational patterns saw no confirmed deployment, as the variant never spread beyond its original Clan operators.

Inner Sphere military commands organized Gorilla operators into standard four-trooper squads when pressing the exoskeleton into service for rear-area salvage and logistics duties. The squad formation allowed small teams to cover a work site efficiently, with each operator handling a different recovery task. Most Federated Suns and Lyran units that employed the Gorilla in this capacity treated it as an engineering asset rather than a combat formation.

Clan formations fielding captured or purchased Gorillas organized them into five-trooper Points consistent with standard Clan doctrine. Labor and support castes made the most use of such suits, employing them for construction and recovery work in garrison zones. The Gorilla's civilian origins made it an unremarkable presence in Clan logistics chains, where it served alongside other captured Inner Sphere industrial equipment.

ComStar and Word of Blake formations organized exoskeleton operators into six-trooper Level I sections. These larger teams proved effective for salvage and recovery operations at major battle sites, where the additional personnel allowed around-the-clock rotation of operators during extended cleanup efforts. Word of Blake Militia units made particular use of the Gorilla during the Jihad for stripping battlefield wreckage.

LCAF commanders deployed Gray Death Heavy Suits in four-trooper assault squads tasked with cracking hardened positions that lighter battle armor could not threaten. Each squad's combined missile volleys and sustained particle cannon fire could suppress or destroy fortified emplacements, light vehicles, and exposed BattleMech components. Heavy Suit squads typically advanced behind Standard or Scout screens, committing to the assault once reconnaissance elements had identified the primary targets.

Five-trooper Clan Points fielding the Gray Death Heavy Suit gained a fire support element comparable to lighter Clan assault armor at a fraction of the logistical cost. The suit's integral energy weapon and twin missile packs gave each Point concentrated firepower that could anchor a defensive position or spearhead a breakthrough against prepared defenses. The suit's slow ground speed made it poorly suited to the mobile warfare that most Clan formations preferred, limiting its appeal to garrison and second-line clusters.

Six-trooper Level I formations of Gray Death Heavy Suits delivered devastating opening salvos when all twelve detachable missile packs fired simultaneously. Com Guard doctrine leveraged the Heavy's firepower in defensive operations, positioning Level I units at chokepoints where the suit's limited mobility was less of a disadvantage. The additional troopers compensated for the Heavy's slow speed by providing overlapping fields of fire that could cover a wider frontage than a four-trooper squad.

The Reaper configuration saw service with LAAF and mercenary squads that needed their Scout troopers to carry more firepower into the field. Four-trooper squads armed with Clan-manufactured weapons could handle ambush situations and chance contacts without calling for reinforcement, addressing a common complaint about the unarmed base Scout. Mercenary commands operating along the Periphery border found the Reaper particularly useful for independent patrol operations where support was hours away.

Five-trooper Clan Points fielding the Reaper configuration gained a scouting element with genuine offensive teeth. The Clan-manufactured weapons fitted naturally into Clan logistics chains, simplifying maintenance and ammunition supply compared to the base Scout's reliance on hand-carried Inner Sphere small arms. Points operating the Reaper typically screened for heavier formations, engaging targets of opportunity while feeding sensor data back to the main body.

Six-trooper Level I formations equipped with the Reaper configuration combined the Scout's stealth and sensor advantages with enough organic firepower to contest enemy reconnaissance screens. The additional two troopers over a standard Inner Sphere squad gave Level I Reaper teams greater staying power in running engagements. Com Guard doctrine emphasized using these formations to establish forward sensor networks while denying the same capability to opposing forces.

Inner Sphere commanders organized Gray Death Scout troopers into four-trooper squads following standard infantry doctrine. The Gray Death Legion fielded its Scout Suits in dedicated reconnaissance squads that operated ahead of the main force, mapping enemy positions and identifying weaknesses in defensive lines. After the Legion's destruction, LAAF units adopted the same squad structure, pairing Scout squads with Gray Death Standard squads for combined light and medium battle armor operations. Scout squads proved especially effective in wooded and urban terrain where their enhanced sensors could locate concealed enemies that heavier units would walk into blind.

Clan Points of five troopers occasionally fielded captured or salvaged Gray Death Scout Suits, particularly among second-line and garrison formations where procurement of front-line Elemental armor was not prioritized. The Scout's sensor capabilities and stealth characteristics appealed to Clan commanders who needed reconnaissance assets without committing Elemental Points to scouting duties. Five-trooper Points expanded the sensor coverage that each formation could maintain across a wider front.

ComStar and Word of Blake formations organized Gray Death Scout Suits into six-trooper Level I units. The additional troopers allowed Level I commanders to split their formation into paired fire teams while maintaining continuous sensor coverage. Com Guard units valued the Scout's intelligence-gathering capability for supporting their doctrine of information superiority on the battlefield. Word of Blake Militia formations that acquired the suits used them in a similar fashion during the Jihad.

LAAF and mercenary commands fielded four-trooper squads of the Standard Suit's incendiary configuration for urban operations and close-quarters fighting. The weapon's area-effect properties made these squads particularly effective at clearing buildings and flushing defenders from prepared positions. Gray Death Legion veterans favored this loadout for operations on densely forested worlds where conventional infantry could hide in terrain that BattleMechs could not easily search.

Clan Points fielding captured Standard Suits with incendiary weapons employed them in garrison roles where area denial mattered more than ranged precision. Five troopers equipped for close-range engagements could control corridors, intersections, and chokepoints that heavier assets would overcommit to holding. Second-line formations found the configuration adequate for suppressing unarmored resistance on occupied worlds.

Six-trooper Level I formations with incendiary loadouts served Com Guard and Word of Blake commands in area denial and counter-insurgency operations. The additional troopers allowed Level I commanders to establish overlapping zones of control in confined spaces. Word of Blake Militia units deployed these formations during the occupation of contested worlds, where suppressing civilian resistance demanded persistent presence in urban centers.

The energy weapon configuration became the most widely issued Standard Suit loadout among LAAF regular formations. Four-trooper squads appreciated the freedom from ammunition dependency during extended operations where resupply was uncertain. LAAF doctrine paired these squads with BattleMech lances for combined-arms operations, using the troopers to secure flanks, clear buildings, and exploit gaps that 'Mechs created in enemy lines.

Com Guard Level I formations favored the energy weapon configuration for its sustained engagement capability. Six troopers maintaining continuous fire without ammunition concerns gave Level I commanders reliable suppressive capability during protracted defensive actions. ComStar's emphasis on holding ground until reinforcement arrived made the configuration's endurance more valuable than the heavier hitting power of alternative loadouts.

The ballistic rifle configuration entered LAAF service later than the original four weapon options, and four-trooper squads carrying this loadout were less common as a result. Commanders who fielded them valued the weapon's effective range and versatility against mixed target types. LAAF units operating along the former Free Worlds League border found the configuration well suited to the raiding and counter-raiding operations that characterized the post-Jihad security environment.

Clan Points equipped with the ballistic rifle configuration gained a versatile ranged engagement option that appealed to commanders who needed flexibility over specialization. Five troopers with effective anti-armor reach could engage a wider range of targets than Points carrying weapons optimized for a single role. The configuration's later introduction date meant fewer captured suits reached Clan hands compared to the original four loadouts.

Six-trooper Level I formations with the ballistic rifle configuration provided balanced firepower effective against both armored and soft targets. The weapon's range advantage over most other Standard Suit options allowed Level I commanders to engage at distances where enemy infantry could not effectively return fire. Com Guard units deployed these formations in open-terrain defensive positions where standoff distance was more valuable than the close-quarters capability of other loadouts.

Four-trooper squads carrying the high-volume ballistic loadout excelled at anti-infantry operations. LAAF commanders assigned these squads to sectors where conventional enemy troops were the primary threat, freeing heavier assets for armored engagements. Mercenary commands operating in counter-insurgency campaigns found the configuration cost-effective for sustained patrol and security operations where most contacts involved unarmored opponents.

Five-trooper Clan Points equipped with the ballistic configuration typically drew garrison and rear-area security assignments. The weapon's effectiveness against conventional infantry made it well suited to maintaining order on occupied worlds, a duty that frontline warriors considered beneath them. Solahma and second-line warriors assigned to these Points accepted the role as necessary, if unglamorous, service to the Clan.

Six-trooper Level I formations with high-volume ballistic weapons provided effective anti-infantry screening for Com Guard and Word of Blake commands. The additional troopers delivered concentrated firepower that could shred conventional infantry formations caught in the open. Word of Blake Militia units deployed these formations extensively during planetary occupation operations where suppressing armed civilian resistance was a daily requirement.

LAAF assault planners designated four-trooper squads carrying the missile loadout as priority anti-armor assets within battle armor platoons. These squads received specific target assignments during combined-arms operations, engaging light vehicles and exposed BattleMech components at ranges beyond what close-combat weapons could reach. Careful ammunition management was drilled into every trooper, as expending all four rounds without achieving a mission-critical result left the squad dependent on secondary weapons.

Five-trooper Clan Points carrying the missile configuration brought respectable anti-armor capability to second-line formations that lacked dedicated heavy battle armor. The concentrated salvo from a full Point could threaten light OmniMechs and armored vehicles that lighter weapons could not meaningfully damage. Clan commanders treated these Points as a supplementary fire support element, committing them against specific hardened targets rather than general infantry engagements.

Six-trooper Level I formations with missile loadouts delivered the heaviest single-volley firepower available from Gray Death Standard Suits. Com Guard commanders held these formations in reserve for decisive moments, deploying them against armored targets that lighter configurations could not threaten. The larger formation size partially offset the limited ammunition supply, as the combined salvo from six troopers could cripple most light vehicles in a single coordinated strike.

LCAF commands operating in hostile atmospheric or vacuum conditions adopted the self-sealing variant for four-trooper squads tasked with boarding actions and operations on worlds with hazardous environments. The suit's ability to maintain integrity after armor breaches gave troopers confidence in situations where a single puncture could prove fatal. Lyran naval infantry units were among the first to receive the variant for shipboard assault operations.

Five-trooper Clan Points equipped with the self-sealing variant found use in hostile environment operations that other battle armor could not safely undertake. Garrison clusters defending installations on worlds with corrosive or toxic atmospheres valued the suit's ability to maintain atmospheric integrity under fire. The additional trooper provided redundancy for operations where evacuation of a wounded trooper was complicated by environmental hazards.

Six-trooper Level I formations of the self-sealing variant provided Com Guard and successor organizations with battle armor capable of sustained operations in environments that would incapacitate conventionally sealed suits. The larger formation size allowed Level I commanders to rotate troopers through hazardous exposure zones while maintaining combat effectiveness. These formations saw particular value during boarding operations and planetary assaults against defended installations with compromised atmospherics.

Five-trooper Clan Points operating prototype Strike Suits would have benefited from the Clan-manufactured launcher system that integrated naturally with Clan logistics chains. The prototype's superior reach and hitting power compared to the production model made it an attractive acquisition for Clan garrison forces, though the extreme rarity of these experimental suits limited any organized Clan deployment to captured or salvaged examples.

Six-trooper Level I formations of prototype Strike Suits existed only in theory, as the small number of prototypes produced never reached ComStar or Word of Blake hands in sufficient quantity for organized formation-level deployment. Any Level I equipped with these experimental suits would have gained substantial fire support capability from the Clan-sourced weapon systems, but the prototypes remained confined to their original operators throughout their limited service life.

Defiance Industries sold the production Strike Suit exclusively to the Lyran Commonwealth, and LCAF commanders organized them into four-trooper fire support squads. These squads advanced behind scout and assault elements, delivering missile volleys against hardened targets identified by forward observers. After expending their ordnance, troopers shifted to a designation role, guiding friendly artillery and guided munitions onto enemy positions. LCAF units operating along the former Free Worlds League border employed Strike squads extensively in raiding operations.

Five-trooper Clan Points fielding the production Strike Suit gained a dedicated fire support element that complemented heavier assault armor. The additional trooper increased each Point's total missile output, giving garrison cluster commanders a meaningful indirect fire capability at the battle armor level. The suit's lack of jump capability limited its appeal to Clan warriors accustomed to more mobile platforms, confining it primarily to defensive and garrison assignments.

Six-trooper Level I formations of the production Strike Suit concentrated enough missile firepower to threaten light vehicles and exposed BattleMech components in coordinated salvos. Com Guard successors deployed these formations in prepared defensive positions where the suit's ground-only movement was less of a liability. The additional troopers ensured that even after some had expended their ordnance, the formation retained enough designators to maintain fire support coordination.
